B4 = np.vstack([B, [0, 0, 0, 1]])\n    return (A4 @ B4)[:3]\n\nclass World:\n    def __init__(self):\n        cfg = json.load(open(f'{SUB}/keyless.json'))\n        self.cfg = cfg\n        self.parts = {}\n        for n in os.listdir(f'{SUB}/parts'):\n            self.parts[n[:-4]] = loadm(f'{SUB}/parts/{n}')\n        for n in ['main_plate', 'dial_plate', 'barrel_arbor', 'minute_wheel', 'minute_post']:\n            self.parts[n] = loadm(f'/app/supplied/{n}.stl')\n        self.mob = {}\n        for n, d in cfg['mobiles'].items():\n            self.mob[n] = dict(d)\n        self.mob['barrel']['parts'] = self.mob['barrel']['parts'] + ['barrel_arbor']\n        self.mob['minute_wheel'] = {'kind': 'free', 'dof': 'rot', 'point': [4.65, -4.157, 0], 'direction': [0, 0, 1], 'parts': ['minute_wheel']}\n        self.mob['barrel'].update({'dof': 'rot', 'point': [2.15, 4.157, 0], 'direction': [0, 0, 1]})\n        self.mob['stem'].update({'dof': 'stem'})\n        self.fixed = cfg['fixed'] + ['main_plate', 'dial_plate', 'minute_post']\n        self.q = {n: 0.0 for n in self.mob}   # own coordinate\n        self.stem_x = 0.0; self.stem_a = 0.0   # stem pull, stem rot angle (about +x)\n        self.cache = {}\n\n    def T(self, n, q=None, sx=None, sa=None):\n        q = self.q[n] if q is None else q\n        sx = self.stem_x if sx is None else sx\n        sa = self.stem_a if sa is None else sa\n        d = self.mob[n]\n        if n == 'stem':\n            return compose(transl([sx, 0, 0]), rotmat([0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0], sa))\n        if d['dof'] == 'rot':\n            return rotmat(d['point'], d['direction'], q)\n        v = np.array(d['direction'], float); v /= np.linalg.norm(v)\n        M = transl(v * q)\n        if d.get('on_stem'):\n            M = compose(M, rotmat([0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0], sa))\n        return M\n\n    def body(self, n, **kw):\n        T = self.T(n, **kw)\n        ms = [self.parts[p].transform(T) for p in self.mob[n]['parts']]\n        r = ms[0]\n        for m in ms[1:]: r = r + m\n        return r\n\n    def fixedbody(self, n):\n        return self.parts[n]\n\ndef overlap(a, b):\n    return (a ^ b).volume()\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    w = World()\n    names = list(w.mob) \n    bodies = {n: w.body(n) for n in names}\n    for f in w.fixed: bodies[f] = w.parts[f]\n    ks = list(bodies)\n    print('--- rest overlaps > 0.0002')\n    for a, b in itertools.combinations(ks, 2):\n        if a in ('barrel',) and b in () : continue\n        v = overlap(bodies[a], bodies[b])\n        if v > 1e-4: print(a, b, round(v, 5))\n    print('--- held tests')\n    for n in names:\n        d = w.mob[n]\n        if d['kind'] not in ('free', 'spring'): continue\n        dirv = np.array(d['direction'], float); dirv /= np.linalg.norm(dirv)\n        # perpendicular dirs\n        a = np.cross(dirv, [0, 0, 1.0]); \n        if np.linalg.norm(a) < 1e-6: a = np.cross(dirv, [0, 1.0, 0])\n        a /= np.linalg.norm(a); b = np.cross(dirv, a)\n        tests = [a, -a, b, -b]\n        if d['dof'] == 'rot': tests += [dirv, -dirv]\n        res = []\n        for t in tests:\n            m = bodies[n].transform(transl(0.3 * t))\n            mx = 0\n            for k in ks:\n                if k == n: continue\n                mx = max(mx, overlap(m, bodies[k]))\n            res.append(round(mx, 4))\n        print(n, res)\nEOF\ncd /app && python3 scripts/sim.py","time":{"start":1794672801536,"end":1794672802095}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1dad58f4a001HNPg4VmWrA55jq","sessionID":"ses_e2535aa2dffeoBkwpXoWeuc2Kh","messageID":"msg_1dad57f8e001t7RsrFZ71zKk2I"}}

{"type":"text","timestamp":1794673201213,"sessionID":"ses_e2535aa2dffeoBkwpXoWeuc2Kh","part":{"id":"prt_1dadbc20d001XvCCPiLfXnIUo3","messageID":"msg_1dadba2f0001tvFCIIZe2o43Zb","sessionID":"ses_e2535aa2dffeoBkwpXoWeuc2Kh","type":"text","text":"## Report\n\n**What I submitted.** `/app/submission/keyless.json`, 11 parts in `parts/` and `report.json`. I did not run the full acceptance test, and I claim only AT-0 as `pass`.\n\n- **Stem** (kind `stem`): one solid with a shaft, a collar inside the clutch sleeve, a 10-tooth setting pinion and the crown. The crown sticks out to x = 13.6, which is past the 12.7 needed.\n- **Winding train:**\n  - `pinion` (free, rotates on the stem) has a 10-tooth spur gear and sawtooth face teeth.\n  - `clutch` is a spring-loaded sleeve that slides along x and turns with the stem. The collar pushes it clear of the pinion when the stem is pulled 0.3 or more. Its ramps let it ride over the pinion's teeth when the crown turns backward.\n  - `crown_wheel` has a ring of 20 rack-tooth pins and a 12-tooth spur gear.\n  - `ratchet_gear` is one solid on the barrel arbor: a 30-tooth gear and a 20-tooth sawtooth ratchet.\n  - `click` is a spring-loaded pawl on that ratchet. It holds the barrel and lets it turn forward.\n- **Setting train:** `setting_wheel` has a pin ring and a 12-tooth spur that meshes the minute wheel. The stem's setting pinion only reaches that pin ring when the stem is pulled out about 0.5 or more.\n- **Fixed parts:** `stem_washer`, `stud_w`, `stud_s` and `stud_click`.\n\n**How I checked it.** I wrote my own overlap checker with manifold3d (`scripts/sim.py`).\n- **AT-0 rest overlap:** nothing overlaps by more than 0.0002 mm³, except the supplied `minute_post` and `dial_plate` (0.034 mm³). Those are given parts, so I left them.\n- **AT-0 held:** every free and spring mobile overlaps something by at least 0.03 mm³ when moved 0.3 sideways, and along the axis for rotating ones.\n- **AT-0 bounds:** all parts are inside the case, and the stem tip is well outside it.\n- **Winding train** (`scripts/chain.py`): it turned the barrel about 0.195 turn per crown turn, so about 5.1 crown turns per arbor turn. That is inside the 3 to 12 range, and it did not jam.\n- **Setting train** (`scripts/setchain.py`): at stem position 2, a 90° crown turn moved the minute wheel about 14.5° in each direction without jamming.\n- **Clutch and click** (`scripts/kp.py`, `scripts/clk.py`): the clutch lifts at most 0.205 over the ramps backward. The click clears forward and falls into the next tooth at about 18°. It has about 1° of slack against backward motion.\n\nThese sweeps only clear overlaps. They have no friction or force model, so I did not simulate the actual rig, the AT-2 hold, the pull and push stops or the full AT-1 to AT-6 sequences. I marked all of those `not_tested`.\n\n**Difficulties, in order.**\n1. The stem axis is at y = 0, but the barrel and minute wheel are at y = ±4.157. An ordinary spur pinion on the stem cannot reach either wheel. I used a rack-pin ring (contrate wheel) on each of two vertical-axis intermediate wheels, placed on y = 0.\n2. My first version used round pins. The mesh with the pinion jammed at once. Replacing them with pins shaped as rack teeth (20° flanks) fixed that.\n3. The click stud ran through the barrel gear's layer and overlapped it, so I shortened the stud.\n4. My overlap-clearing sweep can let the click ride out over the ratchet wall when the barrel is turned backward. The real force analysis should lock it, but I could not check that.\n\n**Ambiguities in the brief.**\n- What the rig does with an `on_stem` sleeve's coordinate, and whether it is carried by the stem pull.\n- How the \"least distance with friction\" rule works for rotating parts.\n- Whether the given `minute_post` and `dial_plate` overlap counts against AT-0.\n\nOutside access: none","time":{"start":1794673197581,"end":1794673201210}}}
